newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold finishes down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold finishes down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market saw two-way business in intra-day trade on Tuesday but ended lower than New York's Monday close following afternoon sales from overseas, gold dealers and traders said.
A continued dollar/yen rally sparked gold sales from dealers on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM), Hong Kong traders said.
"Gold in yen came off, so there was good liquidation," said a gold source at an international bank.
The dollar came within reach of 115 yen on Tuesday to a fresh 42-month high, spurred by the belief that financial authorities would do little to check its advance.
European sales kicked in during afternoon trade, ahead of the over-the-counter options expiry, gold sources said.
But gold was expected to stay range-bound between $382.50-383.50 ahead of the expiry later on Tuesday, they said.
Short term gold lease rates were tighter and players were likely short gold in the market, gold sources said.
"We may see some shortcovering soon," one trader said.
Bullion ended at US$382.50/383.00 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$382.90/383.40 close on Monday.
Local gold ended HK$6 lower at HK$3,526 a tael.
